what: Rapier 0.21 scene queries (castRay, intersectionWithShape) go through the broad-phase BVH, which only world.step() refreshes: colliders are invisible before the first step, and a collider moved with setTranslation is still found at its old place until the next step
evidence: scratch probe: castRay down onto a crate returned no hit before sim.step() and toi 3 after; shape query false before / true after
rule: Never move colliders to rewind for lag compensation; test rewound characters analytically (ray vs capsule, src/sim/combat/geometry.ts). Build anything query-based (nav grid) after the first physics step.

what: Straight-down Rapier rays slip through the West Yard heightfield along grid lines
evidence: 23% of vertical rays on a 0.5 m lattice missed (30235/130321), 0.45% of random vertical rays, 0% of slanted rays; a test spawn at (12,0) got y=-110 and was teleported by the out-of-bounds guard; a mortar dropped straight down fell through the terrain
rule: Probe ground with WorldData.height(), not vertical raycasts; projectiles keep a height() backstop (projectiles.ts terrainHit).

what: Character controller cost on the West Yard heightfield is ~8x the flat slab: movement for 8 characters p50 1.25 ms vs 0.15 ms flat; terrain-only 1.0 ms vs props-only 0.3 ms
evidence: scratch kcc bench (8 chars, same process, same load, CPU time per step); soak breakdown: movement 1.1-2.2 ms/tick vs all L3 systems 0.15-0.36 ms/tick
rule: Budget ~0.13 ms per character per tick for movement on the heightfield; the 3 ms tick budget (12 players + 16 bots) needs a cheaper terrain collider (coarser/chunked heightfield, check FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES) before Wave 2.

what: Nav grid from the real colliders stays cheap if only cells near prop AABBs get a Rapier capsule probe (with the heightfield collider excluded) and terrain is judged from neighbour height() gradients; bounding-circle AABBs of long rotated fences covered the whole yard, exact rotated AABBs fixed it
evidence: West Yard 200x200: 3959 probes instead of 39203 with 0 differing cells; build ~40 ms warm / ~110 ms cold; full probes ~145 ms
rule: Prefilter spatial probes with exact rotated AABBs, exclude the terrain collider from prop probes, and fall back to probing every cell when the world holds colliders the prefilter doesn't know about.

what: On a shared 4-core box (load 7-17 from parallel lanes' headless Chromium) wall-clock tick p95 inflated 2-4x; process.cpuUsage also counts V8 GC/JIT threads (cpu p95 5.9 ms while wall p95 2.1 ms); process.threadCpuUsage is too coarse per tick
evidence: tools/soak.mjs: identical deterministic runs read single-run tick p95 1.7-6 ms depending on load (p50 steady 1.0-1.4 ms); best-of-3 per tick stayed 1.4-1.6 ms at load 6-10
rule: Gate per-tick cost on min(wall, process CPU), take the per-tick minimum across N deterministic repeats (and assert the repeats' outcomes are identical), and record machine load with the result.

what: Over-the-shoulder aiming: the camera ray is parallel to the eye ray but ~0.55 m right and 0.2 m up, so eye-ray hitscan misses a 0.36 m-radius target the crosshair is on
evidence: third-person camera: pivot +1.25 m, shoulder 0.55/0.75 m; test 'a human shot lands where the over-the-shoulder crosshair points' (combat.test.ts)
rule: For camera-aimed players trace the crosshair ray (AIM_RAY constants in weapons.ts) to find the aim point, then fire from the eye toward it; keep the camera numbers and AIM_RAY in sync.

what: Decrementing a weapon cooldown below zero before the first shot and then adding the interval gave a one-tick credit: 11 shots per second from a 10 rps rifle
evidence: combat.test.ts 'auto fire runs at exactly the fire rate' failed with 11 vs 10 until the decrement only ran while cooldown > 0
rule: Only count cooldowns down while positive; keep the sub-tick negative carry after a shot so fractional fire rates stay exact.

what: Bot class balance in the open West Yard (mirrored 4v4, 4x3 min): species even (corgis 116-120 vs cats 120-125 kills) but Warden shotgun bots k/d 0.1-0.4 vs Overwatch 1.4-2.0 and Breacher ~1.4
evidence: scratch balance runs; warden bots died at ~27 m average killer distance before closing to shotgun range
rule: Close-range bot kits need a cover-hopping approach before they are shipped as team fill; tune kits with mirrored lineups.

what: Unit tests that hard-code world coordinates broke when the world lane replaced createWorldData with West Yard (sim-movement: the origin is now a trampoline and the crate ring is gone)
evidence: 5 sim-movement tests fail identically with and without combat/AI/match systems; L3 tests that locate lanes/obstacles at runtime kept passing

what: Instanced TSL particles in 'stretched' and 'ground' modes rendered nothing: the custom quad mapping (perp=(-along.y,along.x); ground +y→+z) mirrored the winding and FrontSide culling dropped every quad
evidence: artifacts/l5-dbg.png beam experiments; fix in src/client/fx/particle-mesh.ts (perp=(along.y,-along.x), ground +y→-z)
rule: When a vertexNode builds quads from basis vectors, keep det(right, up) > 0 (or the material side) — test each placement mode on screen

what: three r186 TSL throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'addToStack')" at VarNode.build when cameraViewMatrix/cameraProjectionMatrix (shared Fn().once() nodes) are first referenced inside select()/If branches of a vertexNode or inside If/Discard in a nested Fn
evidence: console error in labs/juice.html first run; resolved in src/client/fx/particle-mesh.ts
rule: In vertexNode/colorNode graphs use arithmetic blends (step/mix weights) instead of select over camera-matrix expressions, and material.maskNode instead of If(...Discard)

what: FX meshes hidden until their first particle compile their pipeline on the first shot of a match (a visible stall); keeping them visible with instanceCount 0 builds the pipeline at load and issues no draw (RenderObject.getDrawParameters returns null)
evidence: src/client/fx/particle-mesh.ts, onomatopoeia-view.ts; three/src/renderers/common/RenderObject.js getDrawParameters

what: A CSS keyframe animation on opacity overrides the element's inline style.opacity, so the low-HP vignette pulsed permanently and washed out the kill feed
evidence: artifacts/l5-combat.png iteration 1 vs 2; fix in src/client/ui/hud-style.ts (.vig-low::after)

what: Headless Chromium here cannot load Google Fonts (net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID behind the agent proxy) and tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts fails on any console error

what: With 5 lanes running headless SwiftShader browsers the 4-core box sat at load average 15-20; lab frames took 1-8 s, rAF stalled while JS stayed responsive, and fixed-wait probes captured blank pre-first-frame pages
evidence: uptime + __juice.frames polling in L5 session
rule: Labs trigger scripted moments by frame count, not wall clock, and captures wait for a readiness flag; judge fps only on real GPUs

what: Heap-based zero-allocation tests (v8 --expose_gc via vm) need a long warm-up: TurboFan code objects inflated the first 5k calls by ~45 KB while 20k later calls grew < 10 KB
evidence: tests/unit/fx-particles.test.ts; per-recipe scan in L5 session

what: The local death event (bus, immediate) and the Dead flag (interpolated state, ~100 ms later) arrive in either order; a freshness window keyed to 'now' flipped the killer to 'the yard itself' after 4 s on the death screen
evidence: artifacts/l5-dead.png iterations; fix in src/client/ui/hud.ts (deathBy map matched against deathAt)
rule: Match event records to state transitions by record time relative to the transition, never relative to the current time

what: three r186 TSL: vec3(new THREE.Color(hex)) evaluates to black, so style-webgpu glow() (colorNode = vec3(Color).mul(k)) renders every glow part black; uniform(new THREE.Color(hex)).mul(k) and vec3(r,g,b).mul(k) render correctly
evidence: labs/characters.html lens swap on the same mesh+pipeline: vec3(Color)=rgb(0,0,0), uniform(Color)=rgb(255,138,97), vec3(1,.2,.2)=rgb(255,200,172); artifacts/l1-glowbug-vec3color-black.png vs l1-glowbug-uniform-ok.png
rule: Build TSL colors with uniform(Color) or color(hex), never vec3(Color); verify any new glow in a screenshot, not just that it compiles

what: toonOutlinePass outlines THREE.SkinnedMesh correctly in r186: NodeMaterial.setupVertex runs skinning into positionLocal/normalLocal before the outline material's vertexNode reads them, so one merged skinned toon mesh (vertex colors) gets a continuous ink hull with no custom inverted-hull child
evidence: node_modules/three/src/materials/nodes/NodeMaterial.js setupVertex/setupPosition order; artifacts/l1-lab-*.png show continuous ink on 45-bone skinned characters in all poses (zoomies, death flop)
rule: Skinned characters: merge fur+face+gear into one SkinnedMesh with vertex colors and per-part smoothNormalsByPosition; keep crease ink on rigid props only

what: Two three.js math gotchas in procedural rigs: (1) q.slerpQuaternions(qa, q, t) aliases its output with the qb input and returns qa (the weapon stayed frozen in low-ready while aiming); (2) writing bone.quaternion triggers the Euler-sync onChange callback, costing ~6 us per 45-bone avatar per frame
evidence: tests/unit/characters.test.ts 'weapon points where the player aims' (angle < 0.05 rad) caught (1); timing harness: RigInstance.apply 8.6 -> 2.7 us/avatar after writing bone.matrix with matrixAutoUpdate=false (24 avatars: 0.75 ms/frame total)
rule: Never pass the target as an input to Quaternion.slerpQuaternions/Vector lerps; for code-driven rigs compute local matrices yourself and write Bone.matrix with matrixAutoUpdate=false

what: Clearing isMeshToonNodeMaterial does NOT opt a MeshToonNodeMaterial out of toonOutlinePass: the node material inherits isMeshToonMaterial=true via setDefaultValues(new MeshToonMaterial()) and the pass tests `isMeshToonMaterial || isMeshToonNodeMaterial`
evidence: West Yard foliage kept a black copy per tuft; with the ink uniform set to red the copy turned red; in-page check showed isMeshToonNodeMaterial=false on the material; clearing both flags removed it (labs/world.html close-up before/after)
rule: Ink opt-out for toon-lit materials = clear BOTH isMeshToonNodeMaterial and isMeshToonMaterial on your own instance (src/client/world/materials.ts toonNoInk); never on a toon() cache entry

what: toonOutlinePass's outline material ignores the source material's positionNode, so an inked mesh with vertex wind/sway gets a static ink copy at the undisplaced position (reads as black blades/leaves)
evidence: positionNode = positionLocal + (0.3,0,0) on grass tufts: green tuft moved 0.3 m, a black ink-colored tuft stayed at the original spot
rule: Anything animated in the vertex stage (wind, bob) must be ink-free (toonNoInk) or get its own outline

what: Same West Yard grid triangles as a Rapier trimesh instead of a heightfield: straight-down ray misses 0% vs 24.5% on a 0.5 m lattice (0.005% vs 0% random), KCC 0.77 vs 2.42 ms/tick for 8 runners; no character fall-through on grid vertices in either
evidence: npx tsx tools/world-physics-bench.mjs (Rapier 0.21 compat, 241x241 grid, FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES on both); tests/unit/world.test.ts lattice test: 0/158k misses on the trimesh
rule: Terrain collider = TRIMESH of the render triangles (src/sim/world/build.ts); identify it with isTerrainCollider(), not ShapeType.HeightField

what: A hand-built 92-triangle bevel box (flat faces + 2-segment rounded edges/corners, analytic normals) gives the same toon + single-crease-line look as RoundedBoxGeometry(segments=2) at 300 triangles
evidence: West Yard merged props 276k -> 118k triangles with identical screenshots; unit check: closed (every edge shared twice), outward winding, 92 tris
rule: Use bevelBoxGeometry (src/client/world/prim-mesh.ts) for chunky props; 45-degree middle bevel break = exactly one crease at the 35-degree crease threshold

what: 3-band toon lighting turns gentle lawn undulation into dark camouflage blotches seen from above when flat ground sits near a band edge (edge at N.L=1/3, i.e. sun elevation 19.5 deg for flat ground)
evidence: overview at t=0.68 (sun ~30 deg): blotchy before; bending terrain shading normals 40% toward up (geometry untouched) removed them while the mound/pond banks still read
rule: Terrain toon: soften shading normals (normalNode = mix(normalView, up, 0.4)) and keep default sun elevation >= 10 deg away from a band edge

what: Headless screenshot runs die with 'Execution context was destroyed' when Vite full-reloads the page because another lane saved a file mid-run
evidence: tools/world-shots.mjs: 2 of ~40 probe runs hit it; the retry succeeded each time
rule: Wrap probe/screenshot batches in a retry that also rejects blank frames (contrast < 6), see tools/world-shots.mjs

what: Rewinding client prediction to 1 mm-rounded snapshot states diverged up to 19 cm at 0 ms latency: Rapier's KCC resting height inside its 2 cm skin is history-sensitive, and a sub-mm y change later flips grounded/blocked
evidence: tests/unit/net-prediction.test.ts at 0 ms: 13 corrections in 3 s, max 19.4 cm before; 0 corrections, max error 0 after quantizing
rule: Authority rounds player characters to snapshot precision every tick (src/host/quantize.ts) and prediction does the same after every step; a snapshot is then an exact restart point

what: sanitizeInput is not idempotent for yaw (x mod 2pi applied twice is not bit-identical), so validating in the server and again in the Room made the authority's input differ from the client's
evidence: src/shared/input.ts yaw = ((yaw % TAU) + TAU) % TAU; (0.1 + TAU) % TAU != 0.1
rule: Structure-check in the transport, sanitize exactly once in Room.handle and once in the predictor

what: When the authority's input buffer runs dry it repeats the last input, so the next snapshot carries the same ack; discarding acked history made those mispredictions invisible (corrected but never measured)
evidence: probe ?lag=80&loss=1 at 3 fps: 93 corrections with predErr max 0 before keeping the acked entry
rule: Keep the acked history entry until a newer ack arrives, and count starves/catch-ups/drops per player on the server (/stats)

what: Snapshot bandwidth at 12 moving players: plain JSON 36.7 KB/s per client, 64.4 KB/s with a firefight's events; per-connection delta encoding 14.1 KB/s and 30.6 KB/s
evidence: tests/unit/net-bandwidth.test.ts -> artifacts/net-bandwidth.md
rule: Keep ServerMsg as the API and compress only the WebSocket framing (safe: TCP is ordered and reliable; emulated loss is applied after decoding)

what: Input redundancy (3 re-sent unacked cmds) tripled upstream on a lossless WebSocket: 19.0 -> 5.7 KB/s once redundancy is limited to lossy links
evidence: artifacts/net-matrix.md input KB/s column (0 % loss cells vs lossy cells)
rule: Transports declare lossy; NetClient only resends on lossy (emulated) links

what: Playwright page.routeWebSocket (used to stub Vite's HMR socket on :5173) broke the second browser context's game WebSocket: CDP reported the hello frame sent, but the server never received it and closed with 4001
evidence: server log 'c2 closed: no hello received (4001)' + framesent trace; removing routeWebSocket fixed it
rule: Don't stub sockets with routeWebSocket in multi-page net tests; make tests reload-tolerant or serve a production build instead

what: With several agents editing one checkout, the Vite dev server full-reloads open Playwright pages mid-test (players re-join as new connections)
evidence: server log: c1 left / c3 joined as Alpha / c4 joined as Bravo during one e2e run
rule: E2E that must be stable serve a fresh vite build (server/prod.ts), or re-resolve state after reloads

what: Killing the PID of `npx tsx server/...` leaves the node child running, so later runs hit EADDRINUSE and tests silently talk to stale server code
evidence: server exited 'listen EADDRINUSE 0.0.0.0:8799' while an orphan tsx/node pair from an earlier run still served the port
rule: Spawn servers detached and kill the process group (process.kill(-pid)), or run node + tsx directly and record that PID

what: Rapier compat inlines its wasm, so the lazy prediction chunk (1.68 MB gz) duplicates the worker chunk (1.69 MB gz); total ~3.75 MB gz
evidence: vite build: index 377 KB gz, prediction 1.68 MB gz, worker-host 1.69 MB gz
rule: Lazy-load prediction on welcome; switching to non-compat rapier (shared .wasm URL) would dedupe

what: Rapier 0.21 KinematicCharacterController reports false 'ground blocks' (the horizontal move comes back < 50 % with one contact whose normal is straight up) when the desired translation has ANY downward component while grounded; a kart driving at 12 m/s dead-stopped several times per 250 ticks, on cuboid ground and on heightfields
evidence: scratch sweep (hull + round-cylinder bodies, 250 ticks at 12 m/s): dy=-1/60 -> 3-5 stops, dy=-0.001 -> 1-8 stops, dy=0 -> 0 stops on both a 160 m box and a flat heightfield; with dy=0 snap-to-ground still tracked a 15° downhill with 0 airborne ticks
rule: For fast KCC bodies set desired.y = 0 while grounded and let enableSnapToGround follow the terrain; only integrate gravity when not grounded. stepCharacter feeds g*dt downward every grounded tick and can hit the same stalls

what: Rapier KCC shape casts let bodies sink through very large cuboids (half extents 80-400 m) at some positions (e.g. exactly over the box center): round cylinders, capsules and balls all sank; a convex-hull prism stayed exact on the same boxes; heightfield grounds were fine
evidence: scratch runs, body parked with dy=-1/60 at (0,y,0): 400 m box -> roundCylinder/cylinder/capsule/ball end at y -0.07..-0.23 (sunk), convexHull 0.330 (correct); a 160 m flat-world slab sank the round-cylinder kart to y=-0.28 in the sim
rule: Unit-test worlds for KCC bodies should use a TerrainGrid (heightfield) ground like the West Yard, or slabs <= 60 m half-extent; vehicle bodies use a convex hull (kartHullPoints) rather than rounded primitives

what: Rapier query freshness differs by operation: createCollider and setTranslation are invisible to castRay/intersectionWithShape/KCC until world.step(), but removeCollider takes effect immediately; before the very first step no query sees anything
evidence: scratch: ray at a new collider -> miss until step; moved wall -> old position until step; removed collider -> no hit right away; fresh World -> no hit before step
rule: Spawn fixtures (terminals) before the first physics step so the AI nav grid sees them; destroy karts by removing the collider before the blast LOS checks; clearance tests at order 150 see last tick's poses (fine since nothing moved since the step)

what: Arcade kart grip that rotates the velocity toward the heading (speed-preserving, rate g) gives a steady slip angle ~ yawRate/g and never bleeds speed in turns; the textbook 'decay the lateral velocity + transfer a share forward' model spun the kart out (slip ~66°) and killed ~12 m/s² in drifts
evidence: tools-free scratch lap on the test yard: grip 14 -> 6.4° slip at 15 m/s, 17 m turning circle; drift grip 5.5 -> 22/25/26° slip at 0.5/1/2 s, speed held at 14.9 m/s; tests/unit/vehicles.test.ts 'drifts on the handbrake' (slip > 12°, tighter line, mini-turbo)
rule: Tune arcade handling as slip = yawRate/grip; fall back to plain lateral friction only for big slips (> maxGripSlip) and crawling speeds so knockbacks don't turn into forward thrust

what: A flat-bottomed vehicle body on a slope rests on its uphill edge, so the collider center floats r*tan(slope) above the surface (0.19 m at 15° for r = 0.72): rendered pitched to the slope, the downhill wheels hang in the air and a seat computed from the collider floats the rider
evidence: scratch heightfield 15° slope: body gap 0.194 m at the center; fixed by reporting the kart's ground point = surfaceAt() under the center while grounded (EntityState y) and seating the rider from it
rule: Keep physics truth in the collider and send the presentation ground point in EntityState; derive seats/attachments from the same ground point the client renders

what: New world fixtures that appear in every Sim break other lanes' tests that assume exact entity sets or clear arenas: auto-placed kart terminals landed 3 m from the boss arena in the flat test world (3 boss tests failed) and added 2 entities to Room snapshots (net-bandwidth: expected 12 got 14; net-server: expected [1] got [1,2,3])
evidence: full vitest run with vehicleSystems() in createDefaultSystems: 5 new failures; after gating placement on sim.state.room.mode in TerminalDef.modes: only net-server 'rooms are isolated' (a real yard-skirmish room) still fails, by design
rule: Gate map-setup entities on the Room's match mode (or an explicit sim.state config) so bare unit-test sims stay clean; when a real mode gains entities, update the net assertions to count characters (kind Player/Bot) instead of all entities

what: Kart bodies are not combat targets (weapon traces only test character capsules; world rays stop at Vehicle-layer colliders), so kart armor damage is derived from the combat lane's own events: `fire` endpoints that land on a kart body (hitscan, hit=-1) and `explode` radii, recorded by wrapping sim.emit once per Sim and resolved at order 560 (after weapons/projectiles, before corpse physics)
evidence: tests/unit/vehicles.test.ts 'is damaged by gunfire through the combat lane' (a cat's squeaker rifle drops kart hp, hit events src=cat dst=kart); full-sim soak: 3 hits on/by the kart, 0.27 ms/tick for all vehicle systems with 16 bots
rule: Prefer a Sim-level event hook (sim.onEvent) over monkey-patching emit — proposed to the lead; until then keep the tap idempotent (sim.state.vehicleTap) and never re-enter the sim from inside the tap

what: A ground-painted laser (ray from a 2.8 m muzzle down to a dot on the ground at the target's feet) never hit a target standing exactly on the dot: the shallow ray reaches the capsule's axis at y≈0 and slips under the rounded bottom hemisphere
evidence: scratch laser debug: dot passed (0,0,-15) through the dummy's feet with no hit event; after adding a dot-footprint check (feet within r+0.35 m and 0.6 m height of the dot) tests/unit/boss.test.ts 'Laser Pointer Sweep' hits at 1.68 s
rule: For beams that end on the ground, test the dot's footprint (feet near the dot) in addition to ray-vs-capsule; a ray that ends at a capsule's feet is a near-miss by construction

what: Hit-location multipliers can be added without editing the combat lane: a later system (order 560) drains the tick's events, re-emits them in order and regrades `hit`s on a target using the matching `fire` event (eye) + impact point as the exact shot ray, settling the damage delta on hp and rewriting dmg/crit before clients see them
evidence: src/sim/boss/damage.ts; tests/unit/boss.test.ts 'weak point': rifle hull 15 vs pilot 30, chest weak only in phase 2; L3's 33 tests unchanged
rule: Regrade only hits you can attribute (matching hitscan fire event, or a projectile weapon); leave scripted/ability damage untouched — an injected hit was regraded with a phase that flipped earlier in the same tick and killed the boss (16146 → 29900)

what: Boss tuning against L3's corgi bots: bots never dodge telegraphs, so lethality and fight length swing hard on small damage changes and scale sub-linearly with squad size
evidence: headless West Yard fights: blast 44→52 (+lead, r 3.8) took squad deaths per fight from 0–2 to 27–41; final build 4 bots/29.9k hp 187–235 s (7–19 deaths) vs 2 bots/15.3k 276–295 s and 3 bots/22.6k 239–291 s
rule: Calibrate boss HP/damage with headless bot fights but track deaths per minute as well as time-to-kill, treat bot results as a lower bound for human squads, and leave final certification to a human session

what: A many-part mech in few draw calls: one rigid 29-bone skeleton, every part skinned 100 % to one bone via the character kit's MeshBuilder, and two extra SkinnedMeshes (glow materials) bound to the SAME skeleton; parts are hidden by scaling their bone to 1e-4
evidence: src/client/procgen/boss/mech.ts + index.ts; tests/unit/boss-avatar.test.ts: 14,088 tris, 5 draw calls total incl. pilot + jewel, all states animate without NaN
rule: For articulated props/vehicles, prefer a rigid skinned merge (one toon + one glow mesh per color on a shared skeleton) over one Mesh per moving part

what: glow() intensities around 3 turn laserRed (#ff3b3b) and accentHot salmon/near-white after ACES tone mapping + bloom; 1.2–1.4 keeps them red while still blooming (threshold 0.9)
evidence: artifacts/b1-iter1-laser.png / b1-iter1-near.png (glow ×3.2, salmon lens and dot) vs artifacts/b1-lab-telegraph.png / b1-lab-pilot.png (×1.2–1.35)
rule: Pick glow intensity per hue by screenshot: saturated reds/yellows need ~1.2–1.8, not the 2.4–3.2 that suits cyan

what: tsx scratch scripts with top-level await fail as .ts ('Top-level await is currently not supported with the cjs output format') because the package-less scratch dir defaults to CJS
evidence: first run of the scratch fight script; renamed to .mts and it ran
rule: Name ad-hoc tsx scripts .mts (or put them under a package with type: module) when they use top-level await

what: Weather that changes gameplay (slippery grass, sprinkler shoves) predicts bit-for-bit with NO client wiring when stepWorldEffects samples the environment at the input's own rt (the server tick the client was rendering) instead of the authority tick: both sides see the same InputCmd, so they evaluate the same tick
evidence: tests/unit/weather-sim.test.ts 'prediction reflects the weather exactly': LocalPredictor vs authority maxErr = 0 over 20 s through the overcast->rain transition and 9 s under sprinkler jets; envTick() clamps rt to [tick-30, tick] on the authority (cheat-safe), bots (rt 0) use the tick
rule: For time-varying map effects in shared per-entity steps, clock them by the input's rt (clamped by the authority) rather than passing a separate tick through prediction

what: Lowering ground accel from a post-movement world step works by swapping e.char.move for a cached IMMUTABLE MoveStats variant per (base, wetness level); prediction history stores char shallow copies, so restoring the reference restores the exact stats — a mutable per-entity clone would be rewritten later and desync replays
evidence: src/sim/world/systems.ts slipperyMoveStats/baseMoveStats; weather-sim test maxErr 0; 8 quantized wetness levels
rule: Never mutate shared/per-entity stat objects that prediction history can restore by reference; swap in cached immutable variants

what: Deterministic weather/time/sprinklers as pure functions of (seed, tick) built from integer hashes and + - * / floor sqrt only (plus a Taylor dsin/dcos), pinned by a golden FNV hash test, so authority and clients agree across JS engines without sending weather on the wire
evidence: tests/unit/weather.test.ts golden '1649d429' over 2620 values (params, cycles, strikes, time of day, sprinkler jets, dsin); dsin vs Math.sin <= 1e-7
rule: Keep Math.sin/cos/exp/hypot out of values that feed gameplay; use them only for visuals, and pin the gameplay math with a golden hash test

what: A character spawned inside tall grass is visible to bots on its first tick: the conceal system (order 620) runs after AI perception (order 100), and once seen the bot's tracking bonus (reveal x2) kept it visible — the stealth test failed until the corgi settled 10 ticks before the bot arrived
evidence: tests/unit/world-garden.test.ts 'a still corgi in tall grass...' first run: spottedFar = 0
rule: State that another system consumes next tick must be initialized before the consumer first runs (or tests must settle); tracking/hysteresis turns a one-tick glitch into a lasting one

what: Rapier tests interaction groups both ways, so a collider with membership Vehicle and filter Projectile is hit by WORLD_RAY_FILTER rays (hitscan, projectiles, LOS) but ignored by the character controller's CHARACTER_MOVE_FILTER: a shootable drone that never blocks movement, with no change to the weapon or movement code

what: A collider created mid-tick (abilities run at order 450, after the physics step at 300) is invisible to Rapier queries until the next world.step(); a same-tick hit test against it disagrees with what rays actually saw

what: Bots told to rush a target for a close-range ability never arrived: beyond adsBeyond they aim down sights, and aiming caps movement at walk speed, so a 3 s push closed ~9 m at best

what: A 0.9 m roof parapet made a sniper perch unassailable: from ground rings at 30-55 m the whole character (chest AND head) was hidden, while the shooter's aim ray (pivot 1.25 m above the feet, over the shoulder) still cleared the parapet top and hit targets beyond ~19 m. what: Collider == visual on standing surfaces, checked generically: sample a 3x3 grid on every district collider's top face and compare boxTopAt(collider) with the highest box/cyl VisualPrim top (prims treated as PropBoxes) below it. what: A thin prop at sniper height is a horizon band: the swing-set beam (y 9 +- 0.45, 21 m south) hid everything 95-156 m south from a 9.6 m crow's nest, while the 7.2 m parapet corner passed under it and saw 58 % of the yard. what: Rapier 0.21 (rapier 0.36/parry 0.31) KinematicCharacterController cost on the undulating 1 m lawn trimesh is intrinsic: 80-120 us per call (3 contact-manifold queries + 2-3 GJK shape casts against the 8-18 triangles in the loosened capsule AABB) vs 42 us on coplanar 1 m cells, 27 us on a 2-triangle plane, 13 us on a cuboid. Chunked trimesh (0 %), conforming quadtree decimation within 5 mm (0 % in a real room: the lawn stays 1 m), trimesh flags (+-2 %), heightfield (+45 %), the WASM-SIMD build (+3 %, bit-identical) and setApplyImpulsesToDynamicBodies(false) (0 %) do not help
evidence: scratch benches (same-process interleaved, thread-CPU): 28 runners 2.05 ms (trimesh) vs 1.01 (naive 8 m grid) vs 0.58 (plane); real 28-bot TDM room movement 1.95 vs 1.97 ms with the 4 mm decimated mesh
rule: Budget the KCC per call, not per triangle count; to go faster, call it less (analytic fast paths for the common case), not with a different collider

what: Terrain fast path: for grounded characters with no World/Vehicle collider within reach, replay the KCC analytically on the grid triangles (exact sphere-rest height on faces/edges/vertices, TOI to the 2 cm offset, handle_slopes() + normal nudge, snap-to-ground) and fall back to the KCC for everything else. 90 % of movement calls glide; movement 1.92 -> 0.34 ms/tick; qa-budget best-of-3 p50 3.09 -> 1.38, p95 4.35 -> 2.62 ms (28 chars, load 6-7). Shadow comparison on identical inputs: horizontal p99 0.4 mm, vertical p99 5 mm; the differences are the KCC's own 1-2 cm hops at triangle edges and rare one-tick dead stops
evidence: src/sim/world/build.ts terrainFastMove + tests/unit/perf-terrain-fast.test.ts; scratch copy with the movement.ts hook: 325/326 unit tests (the 1 = another lane's load-flaky chat test, passes alone)
rule: Register static analytic geometry per Rapier World in the shared world builder so authority and prediction take the same fast path; eligibility must use the same broad phase and group filter as the KCC

what: The first room measured in a Node process runs Rapier's wasm before V8 tiers it up: 10-20 % slower for its first ~20 s. tools/perf-kcc.mjs always ran 'baseline' first, so noImpulses/noAutostep/offset01 looked 8-10 % cheaper when they were identical; process.threadCpuUsage() is 4 ms-jiffy granular (useless per tick, unbiased as a sum over seconds)
evidence: roombench: first-rep movement 2.38 vs 1.95 ms steady for the same variant; threadCpuUsage increments of ~4001 us
rule: Warm up one room, interleave variants (A/B in one process), take best-of-N per tick index on deterministic rooms; time per tick with performance.now(), use thread CPU only for multi-second sums

what: The low tier was only 4-6 % cheaper because the cost is passes and ink, not density: at 1280x720 (same view) the sun shadow pass is 20 of 121 draws / 238k of 1.19 M triangles, bloom 12 fullscreen draws, prop crease-ink lines 159k triangles; foliage density alone (the old lever) is 72k. Low without shadows/bloom/prop creases + garden tall grass at 45 %: 70 draws / 680k tris (-42 % / -43 %); TDM firefight 258 -> 176 draws (-32 %), 1.38 M -> 819k tris (-41 %)
evidence: tools/perf-render.mjs (GL draw wrapper, pass split by viewport); artifacts/p2/before, artifacts/p2/after, artifacts/p2/tdm
rule: Before tuning densities, split the frame by pass (shadow / scene / fullscreen) and by ink vs surfaces; the cheap tier drops whole passes

what: Quality tiers can switch live in three r186 WebGPU/WebGL2: renderer.shadowMap.enabled is part of the render-object cache key (flip it, no material work); swap RenderPipeline.outputNode between graphs with and without the bloom node + needsUpdate (an unreferenced bloom node never renders); thin instanced scatter with InstancedMesh.count over instances pre-sorted by a per-instance hash (any prefix is a uniform thinning); toggle crease-ink children's visible. Live high->low->medium->high->low: 121/1.19 M <-> 75/753k draws/tris, 0 errors
evidence: scratch liveswitch probe on the P2 copy; three/src/renderers/common/nodes/NodeManager.js:655
rule: Design tier knobs so they apply without rebuilding: toggles, output-graph swaps, instance counts; keep rebuild-only knobs (foliage generation, shadow-map size) few and say so in the UI. A no-HMR Vite server with server.watch: null serves stale modules after edits: restart it

what: toonOutlinePass extrudes by thickness x pos.w (a constant ~1.3 px at 720p at every distance) and every primitive merged into the character mesh gets its own ring, so at 35 m a 12x30 px character turns into a near-solid ink blob: fur, team colour and gear detail vanish and only the outer silhouette reads
evidence: artifacts/k1-before-lineup-35m-x3.png vs k1-before-lineup-35m-inkfar8.png (lab ?inkfar=8 caps the pos.w factor at 8 m by patching ToonOutlinePassNode.prototype._createMaterial: colours come back)
rule: Design class reads as shapes that break the body outline (they survive the ink); for colour at range, cap the outline's pos.w factor (style lane)

what: Combat faces read startled, not fierce: the iris (rim 1.12 r), pupil and highlight (1.17 r) stuck out past the upper-lid shell (1.08 r), so lowering the lids slid them BEHIND a still-round eye
evidence: artifacts/k1-before-portrait-*-fire.png vs k1-after-portrait-*-fire.png; fixed by building iris/pupil/highlight as spherical caps on the eyeball (<= 1.05 r); tests/unit/characters-k1.test.ts asserts the lid shells enclose every iris/pupil/highlight vertex

what: Fur tufts displaced every other vertex and the normals were computed from the tufted surface, so cheeks/ruff/tail shaded as zig-zag facets; with an odd segment count Math.round(u*W)%2 also gave the duplicated seam column (u=1) a different tuft than u=0, opening a crack on the FRONT of the cheeks and ruff
evidence: src/client/procgen/characters/mesh-builder.ts: `tuft` shapes positions only, normals come from the untufted Prim.nrmPos, tuftCol() is seam-safe; unit test 'fur tufts shape the silhouette but shade like the smooth base'
rule: Silhouette noise must not feed the shading normals; any per-column pattern must use (round(u*W) % W)

what: Objective class-readability check: rasterize the posed NPC-tier character at 6 cm/cell (about 1 px at 35 m, 62 deg fov, 720p) from the front and side, dilate one cell to model the ink hull, and take the pairwise Jaccard distance between classes
evidence: tools/char-silhouette.mjs: closest class pair 0.033 at HEAD (hats only) -> 0.122 after K1 over seeds 1/3/13; tests/unit/characters-k1.test.ts requires >= 0.10 for every pair
rule: Gate silhouette distinctness with a number at gameplay range, then confirm with a true-size lineup screenshot

what: Flattened ellipsoid discs (iris, pupil) built with the blob pole on +Y show a front outline traced by only the H rows, so round eyes rendered as hexagons however high W was
evidence: artifacts/k1-iter1-portrait-cat-aim.png (hexagon irises) vs k1-iter3-portrait-cat-aim.png (sphere caps with the pole on the look axis)
rule: Put a primitive's pole on the axis it is viewed along, so the outline comes from the W ring

what: Mouse-aim flight: the camera aim (InputCmd yaw/pitch) IS the plane's command — it turns toward it (heading error x gain, capped turn rate, coordinated bank) and a stall-protection pitch cap shrinks with airspeed, so a hands-off or nose-up-without-power pilot mushes into a glide instead of stalling. The camera answers the mouse instantly while the interpolated plane catches up, which hides the RTT + interpolation delay of an unpredicted vehicle; a small gun gimbal toward the camera's aim point keeps the crosshair truthful while the plane is still swinging onto the aim
evidence: tests/unit/vehicle-plane.test.ts: 360° in 4.08 s, settles on the aim within 0.05 rad with wings level; glide 6.6:1 with no stall hands-off or with the nose held up; stall recovery 0.27 s
rule: For arcade flight in a shooter use mouse-aim + stall protection; keep the aim pivot (camera height) and the gun's convergence ray in one content number

what: Continuous flight collision: sweep a convex icosphere (not a Rapier ball) with world.castShape over the whole tick's motion, up to 4 slide iterations, excluding the vehicle's own (one-tick-stale) collider, plus a WorldData.height() backstop; impacts are classified by the speed into the contact normal (crash > 9 m/s, bump/scrape, or a landing when the surface is flat and the sink slow). A grazing contact (normal speed ~0) must step off the 2 cm skin or the next cast re-hits at toi 0 forever
evidence: vehicle-plane 'never tunnels…': 832 samples at 32 m/s + boost against a 10 cm fence and a 0.2 m roof from 10 angles/dives, 0 penetrations; 'is deterministic': 900 random-input ticks bit-identical
rule: Fast vehicles: shape-cast the full motion each tick with a hull shape and exclude self; test tunnelling as 'crossings of the obstacle plane only outside its rectangle', because a finite fence can legitimately be flown around or over

what: Two test-harness traps cost most of a debug pass: (1) a helper that teleported a plane (setTranslation) left its pilot behind, and the vehicle seat guard (rider > 1.5 m from the seat = teleported by someone else) correctly unseated the pilot, so 11 flight tests measured an unmanned glider; (2) the 160 m test yard was too small for a 20 m/s plane measured for 5-8 s — it reached the flight box's turn-home zone and the measured turns/climbs were really the bounds autopilot
evidence: first run of tests/unit/vehicle-plane.test.ts: 11/21 failed; after carrying the pilot along (placeCharacter to planeSeatPosition) and a 320 m yard: 21/21
rule: Test helpers that move a vehicle must move its rider to the new seat; size test arenas for speed x measured seconds plus the envelope margins

what: Anim.Drive seats the avatar's rump ~0.3 m above its feet: vehicle seat offsets are FEET positions (V1's kart seat y 0.3 under a 0.62 cushion). A plane seat at the saddle top (0.7) floated the pilot 0.3 m above the saddle; seat y 0.38 with the saddle top at seat.y + 0.3 and a handlebar 0.55 m above/0.43 m ahead of the feet (where the pose's paws reach, like the kart's wheel) sits it properly

what: The nav grid is cached per world signature and SHARED by every Sim of that world (server rooms, test sims, the predictor), and bots keep the grid object they got at tick 1: mutating it for one sim's broken wall would open the hole in every room, while swapping in a new grid object would never reach the bots
evidence: src/sim/ai/nav.ts: shared grid ignores destructibles; navGridFor() gives a sim with blockers its own walk/region copy (ground, costs, A* scratch shared; the A* stamp became a global counter) updated in place; tests/unit/destruct.test.ts checks navGridFor(sim) is the same object before and after the break
